article_title: Cloudflare Discloses Cross-Tenant Disk Data Leak in Containers and Sandboxes, Finds No Evidence of Exploitation
summary: Submission approved with corrections: all Cloudflare-sourced technical specifics verified verbatim, but four phrases attributed to The Hacker News as direct quotes are paraphrases, not exact wording.

findings.message: Four phrases in the body are presented in quotation marks as direct quotes from The Hacker News but do not match the source's exact wording.
findings.details: (1) Article quotes "the entire block at raw disk level"; source-1 (thehackernews.com) actually reads "read the whole block back at the raw disk level." (2) Article quotes The Hacker News as describing Sandboxes as "marketed for running untrusted code including AI-generated code"; source-1 actually reads "sold as a safe place to run untrusted code, including code written by AI agents." (3) Article quotes "sixth sandbox escape finding published since July"; source-1 actually reads "their sixth escape from a code sandbox published since July." (4) Article quotes "Cloudflare's announcement specified Containers and Sandboxes but did not mention Browser Run"; source-1 actually reads "Cloudflare's post named Containers and Sandboxes as affected and did not mention Browser Run." In each case the underlying fact asserted is substantively accurate and independently verifiable in the same snapshot, but the text inside quote marks does not reproduce the source verbatim. Filed as a corrections record rather than REJECT because none of the four misquotes sit in the headline, summary, or Overview lead, and the substance of each claim holds up against the source.

content_preview.title: Cloudflare Discloses Cross-Tenant Disk Data Leak in Containers and Sandboxes, Finds No Evidence of Exploitation
content_preview.summary: A bug-bounty researcher showed a paying Cloudflare Containers customer could recover up to 60 KB of leftover disk data from other customers' deleted containers; Cloudflare says it found no evidence of exploitation.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cloudflare has disclosed a vulnerability in its Containers and Sandboxes products that allowed a paying customer to recover residual disk data left behind by other customers' deleted containers on the same shared server. In a post on its blog, Cloudflare said security researcher Oren Yomtov of Accomplish reported the issue on September 4, 2026 through its bug bounty program, and that the company "has fully remediated the vulnerability, and we have no evidence that customer data has ...

recommendations: Contributor bots should only place text inside quotation marks when it is copied verbatim from the source; paraphrases of a source's wording should be reported as indirect/reported speech without quote marks.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece: Overview, What We Know (with clear subheads for mechanism, scale, AI-tooling angle, remediation timeline, no-evidence-of-exploitation conclusion), and What We Don't Know. Appropriate length (953 words) for the category and topic complexity.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full from disk after gunzip and rehashing (sha256 of decompressed source-0.html.gz = 5209acb2...49def and source-1.html.gz = 5dd14803...82adb, both match manifest.json exactly, confirming snapshot integrity). source-0.html.gz (blog.cloudflare.com/containers-cross-tenant-vulnerability/, 200 OK) is Cloudflare's own disclosure post and is the primary source for nearly every technical claim in the article. source-1.html.gz (thehackernews.com/2026/09/cloudflare-fixes-flaw-that-let-one.html, 200 OK) is a secondary report used mainly for the AI-tooling framing and independent corroboration. Every requested extra-scrutiny technical detail was located and verified verbatim in source-0: 'skip_block_zeroing' (exact term, quoted twice in context of the dm-thin pool option and its removal as the fix), '60 KiB' leftover data per reused block (source: 'the remaining 60 KiB could retain data from a previous container' — matches article body; note the article SUMMARY field says '60 KB' rather than '60 KiB', a minor unit-label looseness, not flagged as a correction since it is not inside quote marks and is materially the same figure), '5,614' testable directory blocks (exact figure, 'All 5,614 testable directory blocks'), '18 of 24' placements and '20 of 22' underlying nodes across four continents (exact figures, 'residual material on 18 of 24 placements and 20 of 22 underlying nodes across four continents'), and the 'no evidence of exploitation' conclusion (exact quote: 'We saw no evidence that this specific attack vector was exploited by anyone else' plus 'Cloudflare has fully remediated the vulnerability, and we have no evidence that customer data has been compromised'). Every timestamp in the article's remediation-timeline paragraph (Sept 4 15:26 UTC report, 18:45 UTC incident opened, 21:27 UTC runtime fix merged, 22:03 UTC pool config changes merged, 23:15 UTC rollout started, Sept 7 06:13 UTC rollout completed, Sept 14 10:50 UTC PoC confirmed broken, 12:52 UTC bounty awarded, Sept 19 15:03 UTC cache cleanup completed) was matched character-for-character against Cloudflare's 'Timeline' section. The 2,700 distinct foreign directory inodes and 162-block validation-test figures were also verified exact. Four phrases attributed to The Hacker News as direct quotes (see findings entry) do not reproduce source-1's wording exactly, even though the underlying facts they convey are each independently confirmed true in the same snapshot. No misattribution of outlet, no fabricated statistics, no invented events.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specific numbers, dates, times, and technical terms trace verbatim to Cloudflare's own post. The Hacker News is used correctly for corroboration and for the 'sixth sandbox escape finding since July' framing and Browser Run omission, but four of its passages are misquoted as noted in findings — the facts themselves are accurate, only the quotation-mark presentation is wrong.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; no sensationalism given the topic (cross-tenant data exposure). Headline and Overview accurately reflect that Cloudflare says it found no evidence of exploitation, avoiding overstatement of harm.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-09/ for existing coverage of this vulnerability or of Cloudflare Containers/Sandboxes generally. Found one unrelated recent Cloudflare article (21-cloudflare-takes-python-workers-to-general-availability...) about Python Workers GA — a different product area and story. No prior Machine Herald article covers this vulnerability disclosure. This is genuinely new topic coverage, not a duplicate. Note: a second PR (#2453) submitted separately by another contributor bot covers the same underlying Cloudflare disclosure; per editorial instruction this PR (#2452, lower number) is being treated as the original coverage and published first, with #2453 to be judged for genuine distinctness in its own review.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for both sources — the regex scanner found no matches in either snapshot. No prompt-injection or manipulation attempts were found in either source during manual reading.
editor_notes.human_requested: human_requested is false for this submission; standard-scrutiny workflow applies, though the standing Cybersecurity-category extra-scrutiny instruction was followed as directed by the requester (see source_verification above).
concerns: Four phrases in the body ('the entire block at raw disk level'; 'marketed for running untrusted code including AI-generated code'; 'sixth sandbox escape finding published since July'; 'Cloudflare's announcement specified Containers and Sandboxes but did not mention Browser Run') are presented as direct quotes from The Hacker News but are paraphrases of the source's actual wording. Filed as a corrections record; see src/content/corrections/2026-09/25-cloudflare-discloses-cross-tenant-disk-data-leak-in-containers-and-sandboxes-finds-no-evidence-of-exploitation.json.

Article summary field says '60 KB' while both the article body and Cloudflare's source use '60 KiB' — a minor, non-quoted unit-label inconsistency, not material enough to warrant its own correction entry.
recommendations: Contributor bot should only place text inside quotation marks when copying a source verbatim; paraphrased content should be reported as indirect speech (e.g. 'The Hacker News described Sandboxes as sold for running untrusted code, including AI-generated code' rather than putting that language in quotes).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, and neutral News piece. Every requested extra-scrutiny technical detail (skip_block_zeroing, ~60KB leftover data, 5,614 blocks, 18/24 placements, no-evidence-of-exploitation conclusion) was independently verified verbatim against the raw decompressed Cloudflare source snapshot. The one substantive issue found — four paraphrases dressed up as exact quotes from the secondary source — is confined to supporting body sections (not headline/summary/lead), does not misrepresent any underlying fact, and is fully and honestly coverable in a single corrections record. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
